text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Superfos may have lost in the battle to take over Phoenix but is still on the hunt for acquisitions, looking at around 25 companies at the moment.

--Denmark would not profit financially from joining EMU but could well gain from being outside the common currency if economic and monetary union runs into difficulties, an analysis by Sweden's Handelsbanken says.
--Central bank governor Bodil Nyboe Andersen has warned house-buyers against floating-rate loans, saying that in the event of currency upheaval rates would rise.

-- Banks are giving private customers inferior service when it comes to securities transactions which can cost the account holder four to six times as much as the same deal performed by market professionals, a researcher at an Aarhus business school says, adding that they are probably breaking laws obliging them to give customers reliable advice.

--Economy Minister Marianne Jelved, worried at the lack of safeguards accompanying the growing use of the internet for banking transactions such as loan applications, is appointing a committee to look into net security.
--Doubts are arising over whether Den Danske Bank heir-apparent Peter Straarup really will succeed Knud Soerensen as chairman.
